Mary - Album 1: Bloodlines

Whoof

"Whoof—what are you?"

Musical direction: tense atmospheric skate-punk; heartbeat kick, rain percussion, nervous bass pulse, sparse piano under Mary’s internal monologue, explosive guitars with lightning strikes. Final reveal pulls everything almost silent before a low emotional swell.

[Intro — shattered glass / rain beginning]

Hair.

No—

Fur?

Something just came through the window.

Something big.

Something—

[THUD]

…

It fell.

[Verse 1]
Okay, Mary
Think before you panic
Heart is doing something stupid
Brain can still be systematic

Dog?

Too big.

Cat?

Absolutely not.

Raccoon?

That would be impressive.

Bear?

…

Maybe bear.

Why would there be a bear
Inside Ridgefall City Library?

Good question.

Excellent question.

[Pre-Chorus]
Don’t move fast
Don’t make noise
Find the shape
Eliminate choice

Four legs?

I think.

Too dark.

Fantastic.

Perfect night for this.

[Chorus]
Whoof—
What are you?
What came crashing through?

Shadow
Hair
A shape that moved
Like something animals do

Whoof—
Stay right there
I can barely see

Whatever you are
Please remain unconscious
Until I know
What you’re supposed to be

[Verse 2 — thunder rolls]

Then the rain comes harder.

Of course it does.

Lightning hits somewhere nearby—

[CRACK]

Power dies.

…

Seriously?

Is this a movie?

Does someone cue violins now?

Because this is aggressively dramatic.

[Break — total darkness / rain / heartbeat]

Something breathes.

Low.

Rough.

Then—

a growl?

…

No.

Maybe.

Definitely something.

Mary, do not walk toward the growling thing.

[Beat]

Mary walks toward the growling thing.

Of course she does.

[Verse 3]
One step
Two steps
Hands out slowly

Broken glass beneath my shoes

Another flash across the windows
For one second—

There.

A body.

Hair—

Fur—

Shoulders—

I can’t tell.

Then darkness takes it back again.

[Pre-Chorus]
Heart says run
Brain says wait

Every book I’ve ever studied
Suddenly feels five years late

If this is real—

No.

Don’t decide.

Look first.

Know later.

[Chorus — heavier]
Whoof—
What are you?
What did I just see?

Something moved
Something growled
Something stared back at me

Whoof—
Who are you?
Why are you on my floor?

And why does every stupid answer
Make me want
To know one more?

[Bridge — power snaps back]

[LIGHTS HUM ON]

I freeze.

…

No.

No, that’s—

Hansel?

[Music drops]

Hansel?

Clothes ripped.

Sleeve torn open.

Blood on his hands.

Blood along his arms.

Blood near his mouth.

…

Not an animal.

Obviously not an animal.

But—

I know what I saw.

Don’t I?

[Verse 4 — softer / urgent]
I hurry over
Drop beside him
Call his name and get nothing

Check his breathing

Still breathing.

Good.

Very good.

He’s heavier than he looks.

Of course he is.

Come on.

Help me here—

You’re unconscious.

Right.

[Build]
Arm around me
Lift him slowly
Drag him toward the nearest table

Glass behind us
Rain still hammering

Hands shaking
But I’m able

Get him up
Turn him over

Blood everywhere I look

None of this matches anything
I’ve read inside a book

[Final Chorus — emotional lift]
Whoof—
What happened here?
What happened to you?

Was there something in this library
Or am I losing what I knew?

Whoof—
What did I see?
What came through that broken frame?

Hair or fur
A beast or shadow

Then the lights—

And Hansel’s name

I know what I saw.

…

I think.

I know what I saw.

…

Don’t I?

[Outro — rain softens / Hansel breathes]

Hansel?

Nothing.

Hansel.

Come on.

Open your eyes.

…

His fingers move.

A breath.

Then slowly—

his eyes open.

He looks at me.

“Mary?”

…

Hansel?

[CUT]

TITLE NOTE — STRUCTURAL / FORESHADOWING:
Surface/title function: “Whoof” echoes an animal/dog sound while Mary is trying to identify the thing in the dark.
W-system function: WHO becomes explicit as Mary’s question shifts from “what was that?” to “who was that?”
Mystery rule: the animal-like / fur-covered sighting and Hansel’s appearance after the power returns are adjacent facts, not yet proof that they are the same thing.
